title: Completion-ring shutdown hangs on an in-flight blocking op — cancel-and-wake, and retire the io_uring timed poll that the same mechanism replaces
purpose: Ground: `docs/REVIEW-23-07.md` finding M10 (MEDIUM, concurrency), reviewed at `fd71c5e`: "io_uring / thread-pool ring shutdown hangs on an in-flight blocking op. `io/uring.rs:211`, `io/thread_pool.rs:226` — the worker loop only exits when `in_flight` is empty and there is no cancellation SQE; a pending `Accept`/`Read` whose CQE never arrives makes `Drop`->`shutdown()`->`join()` block forever." RE-PINNED AT `a0359a2`: NO DRIFT on either site. `crates/beamr/src/io/uring.rs:211` is still `while !shutdown.load(Ordering::Acquire) || !in_flight.is_empty() {` and the only other exit is the `if in_flight.is_empty() && shutdown.load(..) { break; }` at :222 — both gated on `in_flight` emptying, and `handle_message` (:258-292) contains no cancellation path at all (`RingMessage::Shutdown => {}` at :290 is a literal no-op). `IoUringRing::shutdown` (:182-194) sends that no-op message and then `handle.join()`s at :189; `Drop` (:197-201) calls it. `crates/beamr/src/io/thread_pool.rs:226` is still the `handle.join()` inside `ThreadPoolRing::shutdown` (:210-231); its `worker_loop` (:240-260) blocks in `job_receiver.recv()` at :245 and, once dispatched, sits inside `execute_op` (:262-300) in a genuinely blocking syscall — `accept_fd` (:391-408) calls `libc::accept` on a listener the caller created BLOCKING, so a listener with no incoming connection wedges that worker forever, the queued `WorkerMessage::Shutdown` is never read, and `shutdown()`'s `join()` at :226 never returns. TRIGGERING SHAPE, both backends: a live `erlang:tcp_accept/1` (the ordinary server idle state) at node shutdown. FAILURE SCOPE: `Scheduler::shutdown` (`crates/beamr/src/scheduler/execution.rs:70-120`) joins the rings owner-only at :84-115; a wedged ring turns an orderly node shutdown into an unkillable process, and because `Drop` also calls `shutdown()`, dropping the scheduler in a test or embedder wedges the caller's thread with no diagnostic. IMPORTANT ADJACENT CONTEXT — BOARD ITEM `BEAMR-IO-TIMED-POLL-RESIDUE`: the IO side carries timed-poll residue that this brief has to rule on, because the shutdown fix lands on the same wait primitive. VERIFIED AT `a0359a2`: (a) `crates/beamr/src/io/uring.rs:24` `const RING_TICK: Duration = Duration::from_millis(10);` consumed at :225 `op_receiver.recv_timeout(RING_TICK)` — the ring thread does NOT block on the kernel for completions (`ring.submitter().submit()` at :220 is non-blocking and `drain_cqes` at :221 reads whatever happens to be there), so CQEs are discovered by a 10 ms tick; that is a timer whose job is to check whether something changed, i.e. exactly what NO-POLLING names as a design error (`docs/design/beamr/WASM-PORT-ARC.md:21`, :68, :188 — "a polling scheduler is a TEAR CONDITION"); (b) `crates/beamr/src/io/bridge.rs:94` `ring.poll_completions(Duration::from_millis(100))` inside `while !shutdown_for_thread.load(..)` at :93. Note the two are not the same animal: (b) bottoms out in a crossbeam `recv_timeout` on the completion channel (`uring.rs:167`, `thread_pool.rs:170`), so it is a BLOCKING wait with a 100 ms shutdown-latency ceiling rather than a spin; (a) is a real periodic re-check of kernel state.
task:
DESIGN STANCE (decided, with one carved fork OQ-A). The invariant this brief installs is one sentence: SHUTDOWN TERMINATES, WITHOUT POLLING AND WITHOUT LOSING THE JOIN. Every backend gets a way to make an in-flight blocking operation END, rather than a way to wait longer for it.

RESIDUE RULING (the scoping decision the brief was asked to make) — SPLIT, and here is the reasoning. `uring.rs`'s `RING_TICK` retirement is an EXPLICIT REQUIREMENT of this brief, not a follow-up: the shutdown defect IS a defect of the ring thread's wait primitive, and the correct fix — block in the kernel on `submit_and_wait(1)` and be woken by an explicit wake object — is the same edit that deletes the 10 ms tick. Fixing shutdown while KEEPING the tick would mean the ring thread still cannot block on completions, so a cancellation SQE's own CQE would be discovered by the tick, and the brief would have installed a fix whose latency is defined by the polling constant it left standing. One mechanism serves both: an eventfd registered with the ring gives submit-side wake, shutdown-side wake, and a kernel-blocking completion wait, so the tick has no remaining job and MUST be deleted rather than retuned. `bridge.rs:94`'s 100 ms is an EXPLICIT NON-GOAL of this brief and stays on board item `BEAMR-IO-TIMED-POLL-RESIDUE`: it lives on a different thread with a different lifecycle, it is a blocking channel wait rather than a state re-check, and retiring it requires widening the `CompletionRing` trait (`io/ring.rs:151-182`) with a block-until-completion-or-shutdown call — a surface change with three backends and an embedder-visible trait, which is its own lane. What this brief DOES owe that lane: it must not entrench the 100 ms. Concretely, the completion channel must be closed (sender dropped) as part of ring shutdown so a future blocking `poll_completions` returns `Disconnected` promptly, and the handoff must state that the follow-up lane is now unblocked and record the trait shape it will need.

D1 io_uring (Linux) — EVENTFD WAKE + CANCELLATION SQE. Create an eventfd at ring construction and keep one SQE armed on it with a reserved `user_data` sentinel; `IoUringRing::submit` (:148-163) writes the eventfd after sending on the channel. `ring_loop` (:203-237) becomes: drain the channel with `try_recv`, push SQEs, `submit_and_wait(1)` (io-uring 0.7.12 `Submitter::submit_and_wait`, verified present), drain CQEs re-arming the wake SQE when its sentinel lands. `RING_TICK` and the `recv_timeout` at :225 are DELETED. On shutdown: the flag is set, the eventfd is written, the loop wakes, and for every remaining `in_flight` key it pushes an `opcode::AsyncCancel` (verified present in io-uring 0.7.12 `src/opcode.rs:677`) targeting that `user_data`; the kernel then delivers a real CQE for each cancelled op (`-ECANCELED`), `in_flight` drains through the EXISTING `drain_cqes` path (:461-480) so `pending` accounting and completion delivery stay exactly as they are, the loop exits and `join()` returns. This is cancel-and-join, not detach: every submitted op still produces exactly one completion, which is what `PendingIoRegistry` (`io/bridge.rs:44-64`) and the suspension machinery assume. OQ-A is carved for the wake primitive shape (eventfd + armed SQE vs `Submitter::register_eventfd` with a separate reader) — recommendation is the armed-SQE form because it keeps one thread and one wait point.

D2 thread pool (non-Linux) — IN-FLIGHT REGISTRY + FD CANCELLATION, WITH A NAMED RESIDUAL. `ThreadPoolRing` has no in-flight tracking at all today (`pending` at :85 is a bare counter). Add a shared registry mapping `op_id` -> the cancellable handle for the op currently executing, populated by the worker immediately before it enters `execute_op` and cleared immediately after. On `shutdown()` (:210-231), after raising the flag and before the joins, cancel every registered in-flight op: for the socket/descriptor ops (`Accept`, `Read`, `Write`, `Connect`, `SendMsg`, `RecvMsg`) that means `libc::shutdown(fd, SHUT_RDWR)` on the op's fd, which makes the blocked `accept`/`read`/`recv` return instead of sleeping; the syscall's error is delivered through the NORMAL completion path so exactly-one-completion-per-submission still holds. RESIDUAL, to be documented in the module doc and the handoff, not hidden: `libc::shutdown` does not cancel a blocking `read` on a non-socket fd (a pipe), and the filesystem ops (`Openat`/`Statx`/`ListDir`/`MakeDir`/`DelFile`/`DelDir`/`Rename`) are bounded by the OS rather than cancellable. The design does NOT close the fd (fd-reuse race) and does NOT signal the thread. Note for the tear: `ThreadPoolRing` is documented at `thread_pool.rs:1-4` as the non-Linux development fallback, not the production async path, so a narrower guarantee here is a scoping choice with an argument, not an oversight — and it is the same posture `DirtyPool::shutdown` (`scheduler/dirty.rs:290-304`) takes today, whose bounded-shutdown burden is carried by the completion bridge instead (`scheduler/execution.rs:88-96`).

D3 WHAT THE DEADLINE IN THE TEST IS AND IS NOT. R1's test is bounded by a test-side deadline on a watchdog channel. That deadline is the OBSERVER — it exists so a hang presents as a clean assertion instead of a hung suite — and it is NOT part of the mechanism: no production code gains a timeout, and the fix must make shutdown return because the operations were CANCELLED, never because something timed out. The house precedent for exactly this distinction is `crates/beamr/tests/function_clause_e2e.rs:50-66` (`run_bounded`, commented "Deadline-bound run (NO-POLLING)"): a watchdog thread plus `rx.recv_timeout(DEADLINE)`, with `None` meaning the pre-fix hang. Reuse that shape verbatim.

D4 NEGATIVE RESOURCE ASSERTION (standing rule 1 from the 2026-07-11 Aion incident). This lane touches an idle wait loop, so it lands with a permanent negative resource assertion in the suite, in the mould of `crates/beamr/tests/timer_resident_cost.rs`: an idle ring must produce ZERO periodic wakeups. The mechanical half is a grep wall over `io/uring.rs` for `recv_timeout`/`from_millis`/`RING_TICK`; the behavioural half is an idle-wake-rate ceiling measured over a wall-clock window with no ops submitted.

requirements.title: RED probe: shutdown with an in-flight blocking op never returns
requirements.spec: Per D3: a new integration test `crates/beamr/tests/ring_shutdown_cancellation.rs`, cfg-split so the io_uring leg builds only on `target_os = "linux"` and the thread-pool leg only on `not(target_os = "linux")` (the modules are gated that way at `io/mod.rs:8-11`, and the whole `io` module is `#[cfg(feature = "threads")]` at `lib.rs:23-25`). Each leg: create a blocking listening socket with no peer, construct the ring (`IoUringRing::new(8)` / `ThreadPoolRing::new(1)`), `submit(IoOp::Accept { listener_fd })`, confirm `pending_count() == 1`, then run `ring.shutdown()` on a watchdog thread and `recv_timeout(DEADLINE)` on the result channel exactly as `tests/function_clause_e2e.rs:50-66` does. Twin legs for `IoOp::Read` on the read end of a pipe with no writer. A second assertion after the green: the cancelled op still yields exactly ONE completion, drained via `poll_completions` before shutdown returns or observed through `pending_count()` reaching zero.
acceptance: Pre-fix RED: `recv_timeout` returns `Err(Timeout)` on the Accept leg for both backends (the shutdown thread is still inside `join()`), recorded as the fail-first evidence with the deadline value stated

Post-fix GREEN: `shutdown()` returns well inside the deadline, and a second `shutdown()` call is a no-op that also returns (idempotence, matching the existing `swap(true)` guards at `uring.rs:183` / `thread_pool.rs:211`)

EXACTLY-ONCE preserved: the cancelled Accept produces one completion with the submitted `op_id` and an error result; `pending_count()` is zero after shutdown; no completion is fabricated for an op that never ran and none is dropped
The deadline is documented in the file header as the OBSERVER, with the D3 sentence and the `function_clause_e2e.rs` citation — so no reader mistakes it for a production timeout
The test leaks no fds: the listener and pipe ends are closed on every path

requirements.title: io_uring: eventfd wake, kernel-blocking completion wait, cancellation SQEs — and RING_TICK deleted
requirements.spec: Per D1: rewrite `ring_loop` (`crates/beamr/src/io/uring.rs:203-237`) around `submit_and_wait(1)` plus an armed eventfd wake SQE with a reserved `user_data` sentinel; `IoUringRing::new` (:84-144) creates and owns the eventfd and closes it on thread exit; `submit` (:148-163) writes the eventfd after the channel send; `shutdown` (:182-194) writes it after setting the flag. `RingMessage::Shutdown`'s no-op arm (:290) becomes the cancellation trigger: push `opcode::AsyncCancel` for every key remaining in `in_flight`, then keep waiting on completions until `in_flight` is empty. `drain_cqes` (:461-480), `decode_completion` (:482-526) and the `pending` accounting are reused unchanged; the sentinel `user_data` is filtered before the `in_flight.remove` lookup. `const RING_TICK` (:24) and the `recv_timeout` call (:225) are REMOVED from the file entirely.
acceptance: `grep -n 'RING_TICK\|recv_timeout\|from_millis' crates/beamr/src/io/uring.rs` returns nothing — the timed poll is retired, not retuned (this is the board item `BEAMR-IO-TIMED-POLL-RESIDUE` half that this brief closes)

The ring thread's only wait point is a kernel block (`submit_and_wait`), and the only things that wake it are a real CQE or an explicit eventfd write — no timer, no interval, no re-check loop; the loop head carries a comment stating this against the NO-POLLING law with the `WASM-PORT-ARC.md:21` citation

Every submitted op still produces exactly one completion: a cancelled op completes with the kernel's `-ECANCELED` (or the operation's own result if it raced to completion), `pending` reaches zero, and `in_flight` is empty before the loop exits
The existing `uring.rs` tests (:645-695, `nop_completes_successfully` and `read_pipe_completes_after_writer_thread_writes`) pass unmodified
The reserved sentinel `user_data` value cannot collide with a real op id (`next_op_id` starts at 1 and increments; the sentinel is documented and asserted)
ZERO new `#[allow]`; no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` outside `cfg(test)`; the existing `// SAFETY:` notes on SQE pushes stay accurate and the new eventfd SQE gains its own

requirements.title: Thread pool: in-flight registry and descriptor cancellation at shutdown, with the residual named
requirements.spec: Per D2: add an in-flight registry to `ThreadPoolRing` (`crates/beamr/src/io/thread_pool.rs:83-92`) recording, for each currently executing `op_id`, the cancellable descriptor of the op; `worker_loop` (:240-260) registers before `execute_op` and deregisters after, on every path. `shutdown` (:210-231) cancels each registered descriptor with `libc::shutdown(fd, SHUT_RDWR)` (ignoring `ENOTSOCK`) before sending the `WorkerMessage::Shutdown` sentinels and joining, so the blocked syscall returns and its result flows through the existing completion path. The module doc gains the residual paragraph (non-socket blocking reads, filesystem ops) and the reason the design does not close the fd or signal the thread.
acceptance: A worker blocked in `accept`/`read`/`recv` on a socket fd returns during shutdown and delivers its completion; `shutdown()` then joins and returns

Registry hygiene: the entry is removed on every exit path from `execute_op` including the error paths, proven by a test that submits a fast op, completes it, and asserts the registry is empty before shutdown
The residual is DOCUMENTED at the cancellation site and in the handoff (which op kinds are cancellable and which are OS-bounded); a silent claim of universal cancellation is a tear condition
`worker_thread_names` (:185-204) stays truthful across the new shutdown ordering — the existing liveness-from-join-handle discipline and its comment are preserved verbatim
The existing `io/mod.rs` factory test (`one_argument_ring_factories_stay_source_compatible_with_the_default_prefix`, :62-87) passes unmodified
ZERO new `#[allow]`; every new `unsafe` libc call carries a `// SAFETY:` note in the file's existing style

requirements.title: Permanent negative resource assertion: an idle ring wakes zero times per unit time
requirements.spec: Per D4: a permanent wall in the mould of `crates/beamr/tests/timer_resident_cost.rs`. Mechanical half: a grep wall asserting no timed-wait constant survives in `crates/beamr/src/io/uring.rs`. Behavioural half: construct a ring, submit nothing, and assert over a wall-clock window that the ring thread performs no periodic work — measured through an instrumentation counter incremented at each loop iteration behind `#[cfg(any(test, feature = "test-support"))]` (the established pattern at `scheduler/execution.rs:837-852` and `scheduler/mod.rs:453-480`), with a signed ceiling and the ceiling's justification in the file header per standing rule 2.
acceptance: The idle wall is falsifiable: reintroducing any timed wait in the ring loop makes it red deterministically, with zero sensitivity to host load (assert a ceiling on iterations, never an exact match)
Fail-first recorded-and-reverted: add a 10 ms tick back -> the wall goes red -> remove it
The counter is `test-support`-gated and contributes nothing to a default build
The file header states the sampling source, the host-state assumption and the signed ceiling, following the `timer_resident_cost.rs` T1 methodology block

boundaries: NO-POLLING IS LOAD-BEARING HERE AND FORBIDS, SPECIFICALLY: (a) any new `Duration`-parameterised wait in the ring loops or in shutdown; (b) any retry/backoff loop that re-checks `in_flight`, `pending` or the shutdown flag on a timer; (c) any `thread::sleep` or `yield_now` spin in production code; (d) making the shutdown fix work by SHORTENING `RING_TICK` rather than deleting it; (e) a `join_timeout`-style bounded join that abandons a thread after a wall-clock interval — the operation must be CANCELLED, and the wait must end because a completion arrived. A polling scheduler is a TEAR CONDITION (`docs/design/beamr/WASM-PORT-ARC.md:21`, :68, :188).

RESIDUE SPLIT, BINDING: retiring `uring.rs:24`/:225 (RING_TICK / recv_timeout) is IN SCOPE and required by R2. Retiring `io/bridge.rs:94`'s 100 ms `poll_completions` is an EXPLICIT NON-GOAL and remains on board item `BEAMR-IO-TIMED-POLL-RESIDUE`; this brief must not entrench it (the completion channel is closed at ring shutdown so the follow-up can block instead of poll) and the handoff must record the `CompletionRing` trait shape that lane will need.

EXACTLY-ONCE COMPLETION IS AN INVARIANT, NOT A NICETY: `PendingIoRegistry` (`io/bridge.rs:44-64`) and the suspension machinery key on one completion per `op_id`. A cancellation that drops a completion, or that emits a second one for an op that raced to real completion, is a STOP.

THE `CompletionRing` TRAIT (`io/ring.rs:151-182`) IS NOT WIDENED BY THIS BRIEF. `submit`/`poll_completions`/`pending_count`/`worker_thread_names`/`requested_worker_count`/`shutdown` keep their signatures; `FailedRing` (:186-237) and every embedder implementation stay source-compatible. Trait surgery belongs to the bridge lane.

SHUTDOWN SEMANTICS OTHERWISE UNCHANGED: idempotent via the existing `swap(true)` guards, still called from `Drop`, still owner-only at the scheduler (`scheduler/execution.rs:84-115` `shutdown_owned`), still panic-propagating on a poisoned join (`resume_unwind`). Changing WHO shuts a ring down, or when, is out of scope.

WASM32: `crates/beamr/src/io/**` is native-only and never compiles under wasm32 — `pub mod io` is `#[cfg(feature = "threads")]` (`lib.rs:23-25`), `uring.rs` is additionally `#![cfg(target_os = "linux")]` (:3) and `thread_pool.rs` is `#![cfg(not(target_os = "linux"))]` (:6). CONFIRMED: nothing in this brief's edited files reaches the cooperative closure, and the beamr-wasm 80-test count and its three CI carriers are untouched. Both wasm32 check legs must still be run and stay green.

ZERO new `#[allow]`; no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` outside `cfg(test)`; no new `_ =>` catch-all arms (the `IoOp`/`InFlightOp` matches stay exhaustive so a future op kind must declare its cancellability); `crates/beamr/src/loader/encode/**` untouchable; NO NEW CONFIG KNOBS — no tunable cancel deadline, no tunable ring tick, no shutdown-mode setting.

Any `unsafe` added (eventfd creation/write/close, `libc::shutdown`) carries a `// SAFETY:` note in the file's existing style; the io_uring FFI's keep-the-buffer-alive-to-its-CQE discipline (the review's own commendation) must survive cancellation — a cancelled op's `InFlightOp` payload stays alive until its CQE is drained.
verification: Full release battery at the final head: the committed 5-leg `gates.json` run (`fmt`; fresh `clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` with `cargo clean -p beamr` and the Compiling line captured beside the exit code; `wasm32-check`; `wasm-tests` with the exact 80-passed carrier unchanged; `tests` workspace-wide), plus the cooperative wasm closure leg and a prohibition grep sweep run through `git -c diff.external= diff --no-ext-diff`. PLATFORM COVERAGE IS PART OF THE BAR AND MUST BE STATED HONESTLY: this box is darwin, so a local run exercises the `thread_pool` leg (R3) and only compiles the `uring` leg; the io_uring leg (R2) requires a Linux run and the handoff must say which legs ran where — a green macOS battery is NOT evidence for R2. Isolation: `ring_shutdown_cancellation` and `ring_idle_cost` 10x each on the platform that runs them. FAIL-FIRST, recorded-and-reverted: (a) revert R2's cancellation push -> R1's Linux Accept leg times out -> restore; (b) revert R3's descriptor cancellation -> R1's non-Linux Accept leg times out -> restore; (c) reintroduce a 10 ms tick in `ring_loop` -> R4 goes red on both halves -> restore. PIN-SHIFT RE-VERIFY at the actual build base (pinned at `a0359a2`): re-read `io/uring.rs:24`, :182-237, :258-292, :461-480; `io/thread_pool.rs:83-92`, :185-231, :240-300, :391-408; `io/bridge.rs:88-100`; `io/ring.rs:151-182`; `scheduler/execution.rs:70-120`; and confirm io-uring is still resolved at 0.7.x with `Submitter::submit_and_wait` and `opcode::AsyncCancel` present. Handoff carries: the OQ-A ruling as built, the eventfd sentinel value, the thread-pool cancellability table (which op kinds cancel and which are OS-bounded), the R4 signed ceiling with its justification, and the note that `BEAMR-IO-TIMED-POLL-RESIDUE` is now half-closed with the bridge half specified but not built.
